n0.speaker: June
n0.text: You've got the face. The 'I'm about to say something and ruin breakfast' face.
n0.aside: Sixteen, dark eyeliner, a backpack full of stencils she thinks you don't know about.

choices.text: "Tonight I'm going to tell the town something."

n1.speaker: June
n1.text: You sound like a recording of yourself. A very nice recording.

n2.speaker: June
n2.text: Is it about the stencils? Because I didn't, officially. FAIR WATER just came to me. I woke up, and I was holding the can.

choices.text: "Where did it come to you from?"
"I'm not cross. I think it's beautiful."

n3.speaker: June
n3.text: From the water. Don't look at me like that. Everybody's heard it. They just don't say.

n4.speaker: June
n4.text: ...You're being weird. It's nice. Don't stop.

choices.text: (Leave a twenty on the table. For paint.)

end.text: June waves at the lake from the bus stop, and then, when she thinks you aren't looking, she waves at you. A short wave. A real one.

n0.speaker: Hank
n0.text: Madam Mayor. Council at noon. I'll be at the back, heckling, as is my civic duty.
n0.aside: He is mixing Lake Blue in the back of the hardware store. Forty gallons a year. Every spring, for the stripe.

choices.text: "Hank, what do you do with the paint you scrape off?"

n1.speaker: Hank
n1.text: I put it back on the walls. That's what paint's for. ...There's a stencil under the last coat. FAIR WATER. In blue. Kids. Vandals.

choices.text: "Keep that coat. Don't paint over the next one."

n2.speaker: Hank
n2.text: You're a good Mayor, Del. You keep things as they are. That's the whole job.

n3.speaker: Hank
n3.text: ...That's not like you. That's... you sound like somebody I'd listen to.

n4.speaker: Hank
n4.text: The first one's older than June. Older than me. I remember the smell of cinnamon when I scraped it. I don't know why I told you that.

end.text: Hank waves at the lake the way you wave at someone who owes you money, and loves you anyway.

n0.speaker: Harlan
n0.text: Hattie! You came. They said you'd drowned. Sit. Have a biscuit.
n0.aside: He holds a green fountain pen, uncapped, over a napkin. It's leaking.

choices.text: "I came, Harlan. Tell me about the sheet."

n1.speaker: Harlan
n1.text: Del. Del. Don't let them put me in the water, Del.

n2.speaker: Harlan
n2.text: My father signed it. I held the pen. Hattie was in the 913. You can't sign a person into a number and then say she's gone, can you?

n3.speaker: Harlan
n3.text: It's in the hymnal. The green one. Don't read the last page.

end.text: He waves at the window, and for one second looks at you with absolute clarity, and says, perfectly calmly: 'Fair water, Hattie.' Then he asks if the biscuits are out.
